content.title: About
content.content: Potato hash browns are a ready‑to‑heat product made from grated potatoes, onion and spices, formed into small patties. They are pre‑fried and flash‑frozen, allowing quick preparation in a microwave or oven.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Hash browns are a staple in Eastern European cuisine, especially in Poland and Russia.
The frozen product can be stored for up to 12 months when kept properly in a freezer.
For a crispy exterior, bake at 200 °C (390 °F) for 10‑12 minutes.
A small amount of vegetable oil is often added to improve flavor and texture.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Potatoes provide starch that offers sustained energy and satiety.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Hash browns contain vitamin B6 and folate, important for metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Potassium
items.content: Potatoes are a good source of potassium, which supports normal blood pressure.

items.title: Low in fat when prepared without added oil
items.content: If reheated without extra oil, hash browns remain relatively low‑calorie.

items.title: Potato allergy
items.content: A small number of individuals may experience allergic reactions to potatoes.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Some versions contain added salt; people with hypertension should monitor portion size.

items.title: Heating requirements
items.content: Insufficient heating can leave the interior cold, increasing the risk of food‑borne illness.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Heat the hash browns in a microwave (2‑3 minutes) or bake until golden brown. Serve with sour cream, yogurt dip, fresh herbs, or as a side to meat dishes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep frozen hash browns in an airtight bag at –18 °C (0 °F). Once thawed, cook immediately and do not store at room temperature for more than 2 hours.
